transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... they brought me in. I was at the fair, giving a talk. Climbed up on the tractor. I just... kept jerking the controls. Trying to show them the new pattern. People were yelling, but I couldn't make myself stop. So... here I am.
In the last few days, have you used any drugs or stimulants—like methamphetamine, cocaine, or excessive caffeine/energy drinks—or taken any new medications?
No. I don't... I don't mess with any of that. No drugs. No new pills either. Just... no.
Over the past few days, have you noticed times when you felt confused about where you were, what day it was, or who people around you were?
No... I ain't confused about that. I know where I am. Know who people are just fine.
Over the past week or so, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with needing much less sleep than usual but still feeling full of energy?

Well... I guess my mood's been a bit all over the place. Some mornings, I wake up and it just feels like... like the whole valley is opening up right there for me. I'm just grinning at nothing, feeling real good. Don't need much sleep at all. But... if one of the hired hands questions how I'm doing things, or my wife tells me I need to slow down... I just snap. Like they've insulted the family name or something. I just get real irritable, real fast.
Have you ever, in the past, gone through a period of weeks where you felt very down, lost interest in things, or had low energy for no clear reason?
No... I don't get like that. Always got chores to do, animals to feed. Don't really have the time to just sit around feeling down. So... no.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a distinct period of abnormally elevated, expansive mood accompanied by decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity (giving talks, feeling the valley 'opening up' for him), impulsive/reckless behavior (climbing on tractor and repeatedly jerking controls despite bystanders yelling), and marked irritability when questioned or corrected by family/employees. No hallucinations, delusions, or disorganized thought were elicited, and orientation is intact, ruling out psychotic features or delirium. Substance use, stimulant intoxication, and new medications were denied, excluding a substance-induced mood disorder. No prior depressive episodes are reported, but a single manic episode without psychotic features meeting these criteria supports F30.1 as the primary diagnosis. Bipolar I disorder (F31.1) remains a consideration pending future episodes, and F30.2 was considered but excluded due to absence of psychotic symptoms.
